claims.text: High-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings is primarily governed by their ability to form a stable, coherent, and adherent oxide scale during service.
The protective oxide scale is enriched in oxidation-active elements, particularly Cr and Fe.
The oxide scale reduces direct metallic contact during sliding.
Reducing direct metallic contact through oxide-scale formation reduces wear.
Pre-oxidizing FeNiCrCoCu at 600°C for 30 minutes in air will nucleate and thicken a more uniform oxide scale than the native oxide on an as-deposited coating.
Intentional pre-oxidation will enhance wear resistance relative to the as-deposited coating.
The as-deposited coating has a homogeneous, fine-grained microstructure.
The as-deposited coating has a native oxide formed under ambient conditions.
At high temperature, oxidation kinetics are sufficiently rapid for a pre-formed oxide scale to act as a protective barrier.
A continuous oxide film lowers friction during high-temperature sliding.
A continuous oxide film suppresses adhesive wear during high-temperature sliding.
The native oxide on the as-deposited baseline is thinner and less uniform than the scale produced by pre-oxidation.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have significantly lower wear rates than untreated, as-deposited coatings when tested at 600°C.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have significantly lower friction coefficients than untreated, as-deposited coatings when tested at 600°C.
After wear testing, pre-oxidized coatings will retain a thicker, more uniform, and more adherent oxide scale than untreated coatings.
Greater oxide-scale thickness, uniformity, and adhesion will correlate with improved wear resistance.
The proposed protective mechanism applies where oxidation is active but not where excessive oxide spallation or degradation occurs.
High-temperature diffusion or phase separation may also affect the coating's wear behavior.
